I'll quote the leaders of this campaign. The queens made their move.

"The portal will open again soon. I can feel strong magical disturbances around it. The time has come, and we can't wait anymore.

Frankly, I don't trust the Sculptor, and neither should you. His allegiance and motives are still unknown. He will help us enter the Architects' world, but he himself should remain here.

If what he says is true, then the first enemy we face will be the guard of the portal.  I don't think he will approve of our determination to destroy his precious Path. And we're going to be very thorough.

Let's do it!"

name.en: Yes, I want to know how the story of Ferris ends

text.en:
Do you believe the Sculptor? You'll have to trust his word.

So, do you want to know what will happen if you follow him to the Otherverse?

name.en: Tell me about the aftermath of the events in the Otherverse

text.en:
The battle with Locus was extremely difficult. But eventually he was defeated.

The harmony is gone... The Order is broken... Locus... Is no longer needed..." the Architect's voce said.

"To become perfect, you say?" Rysina said, crushing one of the Architect's cores. "Oops, I've stepped on your perfection! Hey, what's happening?"

"Locus is self-destructing! Run!" Marianne yelled.

"Move, move!" you all ran out of the center of the Order.

Locus fell apart...

"Oh... may the Light save us. Now that everything's over..." Marianne stopped to catch a breath.

"Nothing is over. Look around you!" As soon as you turned around, you saw a horde of Locuses that kept coming.

"Great Tensess..." Marianne managed to say.

Rysina was furious:

"Unbelievable... That thing! You tricked us! Lured us into a trap! We will destroy you! Destroy all of you, one after another!"

"Funny. If you destroy me, you will destroy your way home. I have fulfilled our agreement. You disrupted the Path, but you cannot defeat the Architect. Leave. Go back. Remember, children of chaos: the Order cannot be changed!" With those words, the Sculptor vanished.

When the expedition was over, the heroes received Zayan's letter.

"Good day!

First of all, let me congratulate you on surviving the battle with the Architects.

It is my duty to inform you that we have studied the cloning system and found answers to all our questions. You may find it interesting that this technology was initially developed on Ferris without the use of any otherworldly materials. The Object - or the Sculptor - provided the energy source for this miracle of engineering. That is why all clones, including pseudo-Herbert and pseudo-Elena, turned into modificants so quickly. Their high intelligence shows that the process of creating a living being from scratch went smoothly. However, the Sculptor's influence on the staff turned to be rather damaging.

Most likely, Tep had learned about the cloning technology and the principles of matter and energy manipulation during his visit to Ferris.

Sarn, the "Master" of the cultists, took high interest in the activities of Tep and his minions. This is how the cloning technology got into the hands of the cultist leader, Gorluxor. Comparing their cloning systems proves our theory true.

Well, this is it. Thank you for all your efforts in keeping our expedition safe. Murk is looking forward to another adventure like that one. He said, and I quote: "If you don't call me next time you fight these hunhurrs, you will regret it!"

Yours respectfully,

Zayan.

P.S.: Herbert and Elena have departed together to an unknown location. I know we probably won't see them in the League or the Empire again. Still, if you meet them again some day, tell them they are always welcome here."

name.en: Tell me about the aftermath of the events in the Otherverse
Ask about the League's reaction to the news

text.en:
This is how Marianne reacted:

"Well, so that happened. I could blame the Sculptor for his treachery, but what's the point? Obviously, we shouldn't have trusted him from the very beginning. He is too different from us.

I must admit I was hoping that, knowing what it's like to be completely alone, he wouldn't turn his back on us. But everyone makes mistakes, and I'm not an exception."

I suppose we are done here. Don't let the Sculptor's actions overshadow your triumph! You have accomplished a great feat. One of your greatest, probably.

I hope our victory puts an end to this story. I will hope and pray for this... Every day! Can the Architects return now that we have destroyed the Path? I'm afraid nobody knows that. So there is no point in worrying.

I have to decide what to do with the Historians and Ferris. The Empire's presence makes things more complicated. I don't think they are eager to share their secrets. However, I can handle this. You should go see Aidenus as soon as possible. He's the one who can tell us what to do."

This is how Aidenus summed it up:

"So that's how that happened. The Cataclysm taught us nothing! We continue to toy with forces that are beyond our understanding! First Nezeb with his vain efforts, and now Zayan with his endless search for knowledge... Ah, at least this time it ended well.

So... The Architects, uninvited guests from the beyond. As Tensess said, the universe only gives you what you can handle. This time these creatures met with a rebuff. If they come again, we will handle them one way or another. Would they dare to? We will keep an eye out for them! The Empire is not vain, so we'll crush them and be done with it!

I thank you for your great deed! You saved not only the League, but the entire Sarnaut. You cannot imagine how proud I am to have a hero like you in our ranks!"

You still don't understand what the Architects are? You've never faced anything like them before. Even demons, while devoid of all signs of individuality, are separate beings… But the creator of demons clearly thought about something like this when he tried to create his army. You are seeing perfect soldiers...

But only a witness of the events can tell you the whole story:

"First there was a Guard who wanted to drive us out of this world at any cost. Then there was a researcher who wanted to learn as much as possible about us... I'm still trying to figure out what the Architects want with us. What is their mission? And what's even more interesting - how do they think?

Look at the way they fight. No one of them stands idly by. They don't just help each other in battle - they complement each other. The attacks never cease. The defense is almost impeccable. When we advanced, they all reacted as one, regrouping and retreating. When we retreated, they pushed forward.

They don't have personal thoughts. They are all part of the same process and the same will." That's what the Sculptor said, and now I'm starting to see what he meant. And I sure don't like it..."

Colossus, the Armada Commander... A perfect tool. Created for one purpose. Now it's starting to make sense, no?

"So it's true. They can actually split into multiple different creatures... Or assemble into a monstrosity. What living being is capable of that? Come to think of it, how many Architects are there? We thought there were millions of them, but what... what if we've been fighting just one Architect this whole time?

It looks like we don't know what we're dealing with. If this is its normal state, is there a limit to its abilities?"

You still don't understand what the Architects are? You've never faced anything like them before. Even demons, while devoid of all signs of individuality, are separate beings… But the creator of demons clearly thought about something like this when he tried to create his army. You are seeing perfect soldiers...

But only a witness of the events can tell you the whole story:

"Can you feel it? Well, why would you - you're not as experienced in psionicism as I am. Even my expertise is not sufficient to fully comprehend the situation.

Well, I tried to read the minds of these creatures, and I could only hear the same thing. Their minds seem to be... connected somehow. They are not just acting as a whole. They think as a whole. And the more of them there are, the louder their thoughts are. What? What they are thinking about? Well, I will tell you later. It doesn't matter right now.

The point is, now the Architects' thoughts are so loud I can't get them out of my head! I feel the approach of something... colossal!"

Colossus, the Armada Commander... A perfect tool. Created for one purpose. Now it's starting to make sense, no?

"Well done! I've never seen you in action before. Now I see that the stories are true. But let's get back to the Architects.

Their peculiar way of thinking and their ability to change their bodies so easily suggests that there are no "Architects" - there is just one Architect. A single consciousness, distributed among many bodies that keep changing, fusing, and splitting? What if this is what the Sculptor meant? If so... well, that's very bad."

Your path takes you further... Through enemies that try to stop you. Isn't that the maxim of your life in Sarnaut?

But there's another milestone. Marianne de Ardeur:

"I have an odd feeling... Like darkness is gathering around us. Invisible, intangible. It's not even hostile. But it makes my skin crawl. Just look at this place - we have nowhere to go if we need to retreat. Everything here follows alien laws which we can't ever fathom. We don't have the time for scientific surveys. We just need to stay alive... Even Herbert wouldn't argue with that.

Very well... Let's cast all doubts aside! We must maintain our courage in the darkest of times. Otherwise, even our faith is useless. No Light can save weak-willed souls!

Come on! Let's find the source of this power and challenge it!"

Cascade, the Hive Commander...

A dangerous enemy! There's a reason his name makes you think of insects. The local residents will come swarming in to greet uninvited guests. It'll be difficult to keep moving.

"The darkness is gone. It's easier to breathe now... Can you feel it?

What a strange creature. At first, I sensed no aggression, but then... Well, it reminded me of Kanian children who cut off the tails of mice and set anthills on fire. Just to see what will happen. The creature was definitely studying us.

Whatever it was, it's gone. Let's move on."

Your path takes you further... Through enemies that try to stop you. Isn't that the maxim of your life in Sarnaut?

But there's another milestone. Ekaterina Rysina:

"I don't like this space. It looks huge, but it's still too small for a battle. And I also have a strange feeling that... Ah, never mind.

I think we need to climb that hill over there. We can't go anywhere else from here - the elven prioress is not great at opening portals, I'd say. Though I can't fault her for it - it's not what a prioress would normally be skilled at. Besides, our magic seems to be working unpredictably here, too.

Alright, let's not waste time. Move! Whoever stands in our way will regret it!"

Cascade, the Hive Commander...

A dangerous enemy! There's a reason his name makes you think of insects. The local residents will come swarming in to greet uninvited guests. It'll be difficult to keep moving.

"Well, I suspect the Architects will soon head this way, and they will be much stronger that the last two.

But I'm already starting to enjoy this. The more of them show up, the sooner we finish this."

The thing is, there are no Architects. There's only one Architect. One mind, one will.

He is his own god and priest, and the crowd that believes in him. He doesn't need anyone. He's whole. He embodies the Order in the way he understands it.

You're in the heart of the Otherverse now. Before you is Locus, the Creator.

Let's return to those who accompanied you on this journey.

"Light have mercy on us..." Marianne was at a loss for words.

"I don't think Light can help us here... What is that?" Even Rysina has never seen anything like it before.

This is Locus. Here matter acquires shape and becomes a part of the whole. Perfection is order. Order is integrity. If you disrupt Locus's integrity, you will disrupt the harmony of the world..." the Sculptor was unperturbed.

"This is not the time for philosophy! We have to stop him!" The head of the City Council was eager to fight.

"You? This is pointless. You cannot break such a perfect structure. Unless... You destroy matter! Destroy the Inferior! Then the existence of Locus will lose its meaning. We... I... The whole is calling me. Do not count on my help."

"We'll manage," said Rysina with disdain, but then you heard the Architect's voice:

"Children of chaos... Why did you come to my world? I am the Architect! I'm the Order! You are going to ascend. Become perfect. Become whole... Like our lost shard!"

name.en: Ask what was said before the battle with Locus...

text.en:
The Sculptor gave you his last instructions:

"Your goal lies ahead of you. Do you still want to disrupt the Path? Reject the Ascension? Give in to the chaos that is devouring the worlds? So be it. I will help you reach Locus, the rest will be entirely up to you.

I will rearrange our world to let you reach Locus. I... The Architect will not like it. Parts of the Whole are already on their way here, so you will not reach your destination without a fight."

Marianne did not go with you:

"Oh, Light, I wish I could go with you, but I can't... Elizaveta and I are drained. All we can do is share with you the crumbs of whatever power we have left. I hope it will help you reach Locus and turn him to dust!

Frankly speaking, I'm not a big fan of landscapes, but... This world is beautiful in its own way.  It has its cold and magnetic charm... And this creature is extraordinary in its... rightness.

I don't feel well. I could use some rest, but here it's a luxury.  I'm afraid if I get closer to Locus, I... I'm sorry, but this time I can only help you with a blessing. This place is starting to affect me in a bad way...

Go! Fight, and remember - the fate of our world is in your hands. Elizaveta and I will come to the rescue if we feel that Locus is growing weaker. But until then, we will stay here and try to hold off the Architects. May the Light guide you!"

Rysina:

"Ah, demon spawn! I have a terrible headache...

The prioress and I are exhausted. I will send my mental messenger with you to carry the remains of my power. I hope it will help you. I can't do more - if I get any closer to Locus, he'll turn me into a drooling vegetable. This monster is way too strong!

So, Locus... That's new. I can feel him squeezing my head... My mind is foggy, and I can barely move. It looks like my weapon was turned against me... Not bad, not bad.

I'm too exhausted to continue fighting... If I can't trust myself, I'd better stay here and help you in other ways. The prioress won't be much use right now, either. She looks like she keeps it together, but there's nothing but prayers in her head. Well, at least now it's clear why the Sculptor didn't want to come here.

Now go and rip that monster apart! Its spawns are threatening our world, and that's why it has to die! Marianne and I will make sure nothing gets in your way!

Let's go!"

The Reaper, Guard of the Path.

You don't understand what creatures you're dealing with. Do they have needs, instincts, desires? Or are those constructs, automatons that have no will of their own? Understanding will come later.

You have only caught their attention so far. But don't expect them to focus on you, because such trespass occurs quite often. But they saw you, and there will be some kind of reaction.

I'll let those who were there with you speak:

"Oh... we barely made it. I knew it would be tough, but this thing turned out to be much stronger than I expected.

What will happen next?"

The Reaper, Guard of the Path.

You don't understand what creatures you're dealing with. Do they have needs, instincts, desires? Or are those constructs, automatons that have no will of their own? Understanding will come later.

You have only caught their attention so far. But don't expect them to focus on you, because such trespass occurs quite often. But they saw you, and there will be some kind of reaction.

I'll let those who were there with you speak:

"That was... intense. We can't underestimate these creatures if we want to survive in here.

Keep your eyes open. It will only get worse."

name.en: Yes, I want to know what happens on the Secret Paths

text.en:
So what do we have so far? One of the Aoidoi lost his lover and went a little crazy - he wants to destroy immortality. It's a tragic situation, but we can't let that happen. We need immortality.

Fortunately, Klavdia has a plan.

"Well, well, the boy is ambitious. He's barely an adult, but he's ready to go after an immortal being. They grow up so fast...!

Alright, let's be serious. The thing is, Kyros might actually be able to get it done. How do I know that? Does it matter? Well, let’s call it intuition. I can feel a mysterious power in him.

To follow Kyros into the portal, you will have to enter the Well of Souls. Yes, that pillar of light which spawns newborn Aoidoi. My magic will direct you to the Secret Paths, the deepest layer of the Planar Rim. I don't know what's waiting for you down there. If you are lucky, you will find an entrance to the Purgatory. You will be the first mortal in history to enter it alive. And you probably won't enjoy it...

But you're used to it, aren't you?"

There was one problem - the path to the Well was blocked by demons who had no intention of letting you through.

There was one problem - the path to the Well was blocked by demons who had no intention of letting you through.

"I warned you... I warned you all! And yet, you are here.

I don't know what I expected! You're nothing but cowards, holding onto your so-called immortality. Well, then...

I'm glad you have something to fight for! It's a shame you will die for nothing!" Those were Kyros's words before he transformed and went to challenge the Servant of Tensess. You had no other choice but to follow him.

You made it to Purgatory before Kyros. The goblin innkeeper dropped his jaw when he saw you.

"What? I smell living flesh! What are you doing here?! You can't be here!"

And when you tried to warn him, he scoffed, "Kyros-shmyros! You can't just walk in here! It's Purgatory, not a market square!

There are no Kyroses in this place. I'd remember a name like that...

Wait. What's this noise?"

And the walls of Purgatory fell when Kyros made his way in. Gripping his scythe, he lunged at the Servant of Tensess.

Well, you won in the end. Kyros was defeated.

There are a lot of amazing creatures in this world, and you've never seen most of them. But the Secret Paths, and those who live here, are a different story. You were "lucky" to run into Simargl, the Guardian of Secret Paths.

This overgrown white six-legged cat loves riddles and games. She reminds me of one of our mutual acquaintances. However, games on the Secret Paths are very dangerous, and if you go the wrong way, you can be lost forever.

"Sweet sparks are coming to my Prism! They were lost on the Secret Paths... Poor things!

Will you play a game with me, sparks? If you win, I'll let you go. If I win, you will be wandering forever in my worlds. For I am the lock, and I am the key, and I make the rules on the Secret Paths!"

Fortunately, you managed to outwit this creature. Or else you'd be stuck somewhere on the Planar Rim.

The flow of time is frozen in this place. It seems that even the heart fell silent, following the rhythm of the Planar Rim. Its last beat was a century ago, and it'll be another century before the next one.

Your enemy is waiting in the middle of the Bridge of Times.

I think you remember the stranger you met with Kyros when you caught up with him on the island of the centaurs. As you understand, our friend Aoidos has not yet mastered the art of traveling across the Planar Rim. Someone carefully guided him to his goal, but who were they...?

Well, make a guess. I'm afraid Nihaz found a loophole and came back to Sarnaut. We don't know much about the Wanderer. This dark mage does not belong in Sarnaut. He is an eternal wanderer, and he can travel between worlds.

I hope he hasn't done anything to the Well of Souls. Otherwise, terrible troubles will come upon us.

"You've made it here after all... Your creator must have put a lot of obstinacy in you. Don't forget that obstinacy had led him to imprisonment, and then to madness. And you might end up like him!" said the mage when he met you on the Bridge of Time.

Fortunately, you defeated him. Alas, you had little time: Kyros found the way to Purgatory.

"Ahh... You're late anyway... The Dark Blade has been tempered in blood, and nothing can stop it!" exclaimed the Wanderer before disappearing.

With the death of the Wanderer, time resumes its normal course. The dark skies of Secret Paths are clearing.

The gates of Purgatory are wide open - all you need to do is cross the Bridge of Times.

name.en: Yes, I want to know what happens in Tep's Pyramid.

text.en:
What is insanity? They say insanity is doing the same thing over and over again. And expecting different results. If so, then Tep is clearly insane...

After all, he had to resurrect over and over again for thousands of years. Really, I could never understand why people are drawn to him... After all, only a madman can believe this maniac.

Do you know how Tep keeps his cultists? First, he promises them the world, eternal life, and all that. Then he demands an entrance fee and a monthly tax - part of the Spark's radiance. Finally, the newcomer is sent to recruit other unfortunates. Brought a new fool into the cult? Get a sip of his life. If you screwed up, you pay with your own. Such is Tep's Pyramid...

name.en: Tell me about the aftermath of the events in Tep's Pyramid

text.en:
You haven't had enough? Shouldn't we stop here? Oh, well.

Before the heroes could recover from the shock after Klavdia's disappearance, the ghosts of Skrakan and Nezeb appeared before them! They had been imprisoned in Tep's Pyramid all this time...

You only had to question them...

This is what Skrakan said:

 "Light... Sounds... Life... I haven't felt all this in such a long time!

Don't be afraid of me. I'm a captive of Tep's, like the other prisoners of this pyramid. I spent a few years bound by a powerful spell once, yet that was nothing compared to the absolute power this mad warlock has over defenseless Sparks!

Allow me not to say my name. It's tarnished forever! What we thought of as a great triumph proved a great disaster. I did not learn from my mistake, and the blood of innocents was spilled again because of me... The Great Astral Campaign... The Great Bloody Campaign... No, don't ask me anything! Those are deeds of a distant past, and I've had enough time to realize the depth of my disgrace. And my tormentor Tep contributed greatly to that. When he got a new body, he often tormented my incorporeal spirit with tales of his great triumph that our mistake made possible.

You already know a lot about the Seals that we knew as the Sources. A lot, but not everything!

It will be a while before I feel brave enough to face the descendants of those who perished because of me. You will be the one to tell them this. Use my knowledge as you deem appropriate, but don't make our mistake again. Don't let your pride cloud your mind!

Tep... I'm still amazed at the power in his madness. Who would have thought that one day the once-dead man would try to drag the whole world into oblivion?

It scares me how easily Tep dealt with his enemies. How easily he created a whole world, albeit an illusory one. If it's not divine power, then it's something very close to one. And I think I know what the secret of his incredible power is. It's the Seals!

I know that Tep experimented with a small fragment of one of the Seals and drew power from it to create his Plague. This is one of the manifestations of the Sources - the manifestation of death. But the Pyramid… Illusions, energy, matter, the creation of new life and the impact on the mind. A full set of powers available to the Great Mages, and on top of that, the most elaborate curses. No, I don't believe that Tep could achieve all this alone. Until recently, he was just a body howling in pain, stuck between life and death. I'm sure Tep had help! And it was someone who knows everything about our Great Experiment."

name.en: Ask what Skrakan said about the Grand Experiment

text.en:
"I think you have already guessed the bitter truth, so I'm just going to dispel all remaining doubts. The Grand Experiment and the Cataclysm are one and the same!

Blinded by our pride, we searched for ways to increase our power. We found the Sources. We had no idea what the Seals were and why they were important. Every one of the Great Mages wanted only one thing - power, free power! We tried to master the power of the Seals. When our first attempt failed, we continued to attack the Source Seal again and again with the most powerful spells until it cracked and released its power into the world. Power against power, you know? The Seals gave way, the world's shell cracked, and the Astral put an end to the Sarnaut as I knew it. You know the rest - the world in ruins, the legend of the Patrons, the Great Mages being the last stronghold of order in a realm of chaos... But I see that you don't believe my words.

I may be dead, but I cherish hope that my death at least partly made up for the great debt of all the Great Mages since the Cataclysm!

I don't expect you to believe me. I wouldn't believe me either. But I have proof.

I recorded the Grand Experiment in detail for future generations, but I never had the courage to reveal the truth. I know that's cowardice, but the truth would mean the end of our world as we know it. A few mages were killed by mad commoners in the first years after the Cataclysm. Then the rebels died themselves, so there was no one left to protect their allods from the Astral. Just imagine what would've happened if I'd announced that it'd been us, the Great Mages, who destroyed this world? No, I could never do that. Yet the truth... The truth had to be preserved.

There is a cache in the tower in the center of Novograd. There's a column in a hall on the second story, the floor dented at its foundation. Utter the words I'll tell you next to that column, and the cache will open. Use the papers inside as you deem appropriate, but remember that the truth can kill faster than the sharpest sword!"

The heroes took the papers to Lovewise Catfish. He was shocked:

"What? What's in these papers? Let me see...

I can't believe my eyes! Those mages caused the Cataclysm and almost destroyed the whole world? I don't believe it! I don't want to believe it! But the journal...

You know, here's what I think. It doesn't matter what happened. The Great Mages paid for their mistake already by becoming prisoners of their own allods.  It's not for you or me to judge them.

I'll keep these papers, put them on the top shelf, and do my best to forget all about them. The people believe in the wisdom and power of the Great Mages, and that faith supports them better than any true knowledge. Sometimes it's better not to know. It's enough to simply believe."

So you still had questions: who helped Tep gain divine power? Where did Klavdia go and why?

You haven't had enough? Shouldn't we stop here? Oh, well.

Before the heroes could recover from the shock after Klavdia's disappearance, the ghosts of Skrakan and Nezeb appeared before them! They had been imprisoned in Tep's Pyramid all this time...

You only had to question them...

This is what Nezeb said:

"Freedom! I'm finally free again! My body might be destroyed, but my spirit is stronger than ever!

Accursed Tep! Our Great Astral Campaign got us nowhere, and to make matters worse, we couldn't even die a proper death either. Years of captivity spent in that pyramid felt like an eternity to me!

Only dreams of revenge helped me hang onto my sanity. Every hour, every minute I'd dream of wiping the floor with the mad necromancer. Alas, my dreams were not destined to come true: a ghost's abilities are limited. I'll have to be satisfied with the fact that it was the Empire that took down my enemy.

I won't tell you my name. It was foolish and reckless to go along with Skrakan's crazy scheme. I'm disgraced by my ignominious and pointless death, but no one must know of my disgrace. To the Imperials, all who died in the astral campaign are heroes. Let it stay that way. The good of the Empire is above personal ambition!

But that's not what I want to talk to you about. I'm concerned about the Sources you know as the Seals.

While I was held in the Pyramid, I had plenty of time to think. After he got himself a new body, Tep would often taunt us, the bodiless ones. So I had enough food for thought. And some of my conclusions are disturbing.

I hope you're brave enough to challenge the forces that killed me. You and the other heroes are responsible for the future of our great realm. Honor the memory of those who gave their lives for the Empire!

Tep... I'm still amazed at the power in his madness. Who would have thought that one day the once-dead man would try to drag the whole world into oblivion?

It scares me how easily Tep dealt with his enemies. How easily he created a whole world, albeit an illusory one. If it's not divine power, then it's something very close to one. And I think I know what the secret of his incredible power is. It's the Seals!

text.en:
"I think you have already guessed the bitter truth, so I'm just going to dispel all remaining doubts. The Grand Experiment and the Cataclysm are one and the same!

When our first attempt failed, we continued to attack the Source Seal again and again with the most powerful spells until it cracked and released its power into the world. I don't expect you to believe me. I wouldn't believe me either. But I have proof.

There's a cache in Yasker’s Tower. I doubt it has been discovered - I made sure it was difficult to find. Find a small bookshelf with an obscene word scratched into the side of it. Don't worry - I don't think anyone has been able to paint over it. Read it backwards, and the cache will open. Take the documents inside and do what you think is best with them. You can burn them - or you can publish them. But consider the consequences of your decision carefully. Remember: the future of the Empire depends on you!

The heroes took the papers to Mark Staritsin. He was shocked:

"Well, I'll be... This is huge! So the Great Mages have been lying to everyone for centuries? First, they almost destroyed our world, and now... What now? They are trapped on the pitiful pieces of land we know as the allods. Knowing they live forever... Indeed, their self-imposed punishment is a cruel one. Eternal imprisonment - and a voluntary one at that!

I guess it would've been better if you'd never found these records. They can divide the Empire and turn the people against Yasker and the other Great Mages... That would mean the end of this world! There would be no holding back the demon army!

I won't let that happen! For the Empire's sake, I'll take these papers from you and hide them in a deposit box in the deepest bunker. Trust me, that would be best. Knowledge is too dangerous, especially when it contradicts faith."

So you still had questions: who helped Tep gain divine power? Where did Klavdia go and why?

After some heroics, you managed to activate the elevator in the laboratory. You just had to go up.

I'll quote Klavdia here:

"All you have to do is to go up to the top of the Pyramid and fight Tep. The battle would be the stuff of legends! If someone lives to tell them, that is.

But I feel a sense of misgiving. The elevator is the only way to get to the top, which makes it the perfect place for an ambush. At least for your group. The enemy will probably strike as soon as you get there! So I'll go first and draw them away. I have my own tricks so I'll be there before you.

Oh, I almost forgot! Remember that three-headed thing at the ship graveyard? Tep has let his pet dragon loose - the one you fought earlier. And it might take an interest in the elevator as it moves up. So keep your eyes open - you never know where trouble might come from.

Alright, wish me luck. See you at the top of the Pyramid!

Oh, it's a pity that words cannot convey the beauty of the ensuing battle. Defeating this creature was far from easy. You had to be cunning and resourceful.

When you got to the top, you met Klavdia.

"It looks like I overestimated my powers. I didn't stand a chance!

Tep is smart. He knew I'd be the first to get here, so that ambush wasn't laid for you. They were waiting for me. He planned for that three-headed monster to destroy you when you were moving up. And he wanted to catch me alive! I dread to imagine what would've happened.

Oh... Everything hurts! With these injuries I can't help you in the next battle. You'll have to fight Tep without me..."

I'll quote Klavdia. She told you this in Tep's Pyramid:

"Does the name of Celestine de Ardeur mean anything to you? No? And she dreams of wreaking vengeance on you. Because of you, she became a cripple confined to the Pyramid forever.

That's Nihil. Yes, you fought her to save the mechanic Charles de Doucer. Yet I remember her as a young and enthusiastic elven girl. Simeon de Ardeur predicted a great future for her! Well, I guess it came true...

I think I know how Tep managed to win Celestine over. She'd always had an interest in machinery, so her thirst for knowledge outweighed her love for her House. She created Caesaria, the artificial intelligence controlling the Darkblood Citadel. And now Nihil has become an AI herself.

Tep has severely punished her for the defeat. Tep managed to return Nihil's spark into her dead body. He made her his loyal watchdog, damaged but still extremely dangerous. Tep has integrated the body of his disgraced servant into the control mechanisms of the Pyramid. She won't let anyone harm her brainchild. Can you imagine how she must be suffering. She no longer has any notion of the Beauty.

Please make her death as painless possible. I feel sorry for her. No one deserves this..."

So... You managed to defeat her and disable the mechanisms she controlled. This is how Klavdia reacted to her death:

"You wouldn't wish it on your worst enemy, being confined to your creation and having to watch as it gets destroyed...

Nihil can finally rest in peace... I wish I'd gotten through to her after our victory. Celestine's brilliant mind could have done so much for the Beauty that's so important to the Elves. But what's done cannot be undone. Now you should go to the enemy's den and eliminate this threat to the world."

Ha-ha! You're just in time to share in my triumph! The world is full of imperfect creatures… Rotting flesh, and dead thoughts...

I was once loved. I was once hated. That world has long died, turned to dust. There's no one who can comprehend the greatness of my ideas. Only dust and bones are around me...

The centuries of pain have taught me to listen to the music of the Universe. I finally understand the brilliant plan of the Creator! Now that I'm as powerful as the gods, I can fulfill it!

Do you really think you can challenge someone who has absorbed the ocean of pain and tempered his spirit in it?

He who understands the essence of creation does not need this weak flesh!

Look into your future. Isn't it wonderful?

Living flesh is imperfect. You will see that yourselves!"

And once you gave a good thrashing to his first body, it started releasing Tep's Plague.

"That was foolish... My old body is still infected with my plague. And you just let it out!"

Fortunately for you, Klavdia showed up then:

"Hang on! I was able to cure the plague before, and I'll do it again!"

And the sorceress fought alongside you. Tep was seemingly defeated when suddenly multiple Sparks started filling him with power.

"I will take your Sparks, and they will shine, glorifying me!" the villain exclaimed, and then...

...then Klavdia intercepted his own Spark.

"You wouldn't dare! No!!

Tep's last words echoed through the hall.

"At last! I've been waiting for this for so long! A power equal to gods' might is now in my hands. It's mine! You hear that? Mine!

I'm sorry, but I'll have to leave you. Farewell, heroes! Greatness awaits!"

And the red-haired sorceress vanished, leaving the confused heroes behind. The end!

Do you see now why I don't like this story?

name.en: Yes, I want to know what happens in the Tungar Camp

text.en:
You are not dealing with mad gods or feisty sorceresses this time! You are on the forgotten Ferris, where the Tungars live in the ice. These savages worship their barbarian deities. Strength is the only thing they respect.

You managed to piss them off. You captured their camp, insulted their deities, and beat up their leader. They can't wait to pay you back. Alas, the Historians are no match for you, and as soon as you leave the camp, it will be defenseless. And if the Tungars break in here, they will slaughter everyone.

The solution: strike first. Go to their camp and deal with them.

name.en: Tell me about the aftermath of the events in the Tungar Camp

text.en:
This fight did not decide the fate of the world. But it was important for your expedition. After covering the rear, you could move on. All you had to do was get past the ice barrier in the cave.

And the Tungars, now led by Tyk, Myk and Pyk, have become your friends. For the most part. Of course, there were other tribes who dreamed of the "upper world"... They left when an opportunity presented itself...

Since such conversations usually end with discussions about the fate of the world and the secrets of the universe, why break the tradition?

I'll give you a hint.

What did you see? On the bottom of the lake? A mysterious meteorite shard? We'll talk about that later.

Besides, perhaps you were curious about the fact that the Pridens came here from their homeland, Howlem. Let me tell you another fact: Ferris and Howlem have a number of common endemics. That is, creatures that live only there.

And one last observation - to the west of here, in Dragon Bay, there is a skeleton of a Great Dragon.

You see what I'm getting at?

name.en: Tell me about the Chief Booka-Booka

text.en:
The Tribe Chief Booka-Booka. It's a funny name. But that savage is far from funny. Riding on his stinking yak, he is formidable primarily because he can gather a huge crowd under his command.

I'll let our scout speak:

"It's about time we beheaded the most stubborn Tungar on this allod. As I expected, Chief Booka-Booka is not as revered as he used to be. Tyk and Pyk consider you their leader, for example. Together with Myk, they will help you in this fight. You probably understand that their help is worth a lot.

Still, be careful. Booka is a really strong enemy, eysh! He is brave and daring, like a bird that protects its nest from a lynx. When he was young, he tamed and saddled a wild yak by himself! You know, the Tungars are terrified of yaks. And as far as I know, he killed the previous chief and rightfully took his place. Such are their traditions!

I doubt you can take him alive. This hunhurr definitely won't be asking for mercy."

That's the way they are. Eysh!

Don't worry. That Tungar was strong, but you and your allies defeated him.

"Excellent, eysh! The Tungars will finally get off our back without their barking chief. Things will get better now. Of course, little groups of crazy fanatics will keep attacking us from time to time, but we'll have no trouble fighting them off.

But no more games. Our next enemy will be more serious."

Those were Maas-Tyna's words.

name.en: Tell me about the ancient mammoth Toros

text.en:
Well, you already know the power of faith. Imagine this: at the dawn of this world, there were almost no deities here. The first appeared when the energies of Creation, spread by Sarn, gave rise to anomalies that manifested in the form of the first elementals. But the power of faith made them real gods! Primitive tribes prayed to their idols, and that made them stronger.

We have a typical example. I don’t even know if some kind of spirit possessed the mammoth, or the mammoth became something else...

That's what a Priden said:

"That creature the Tungars worship actually exists, eysh! The ancient beast dwells in one of the deepest Northern caves. Myk told me they call it Toros.

Ay-hya... I took it for a regular old mammoth at first. But the body of this beast is obviously possessed by some hunhurr, eysh! It can control the power of cold and wind. The Tungars bring it offerings. They believe it will help it live forever, and it will annihilate all their enemies. And you know what the power of faith can do, don't you?

You will have to eliminate not only the mammoth, but also that crazy Tungar cult. Tyk, Pyk, and even Myk have agreed to help you, even though the thought of facing Toros scares them to death. Follow their example! Be brave and slay the monster!

Ferris has never seen a hunt like that, eysh!"

The fight was difficult, but you won.

"We all felt its death. Can you feel that, too, zoor? As if it has become warmer. And brrighter. And I can breathe more freely. What if it was actually... a god? Or something like that. It's a shame we will never find out.

But I'm happy that Toros is gone. That's one less threat, eysh!"

name.en: Tell me about the Tungar champions

text.en:
Tyk is the best warrior, Pyk is the best hunter, and Myk is the best shaman.

Let's hear Maas-Tyna the Light-Footed:

"Believe it or not, there are decent warriors among the Tungars, eysh! They will try to duel you, and they will fight till their last gasp. They are the last hope of these savages. All Tungars are now hiding behind their champions.

They know you are coming, and they are ready to face you. The best warrior, the best hunter, and the best shaman. Defeat them - and the Tungars will scatter in terror! Will you do that?

But don't kill them, no! Show mercy. The spirits say those champions might turn out to be useful. A true hunter doesn't spill blood needlessly!"

And she's right. Don't try to take someone else's life. Don't do anything you can't fix later.

After you defeated them, these champions defected to you. I told you they respect strength. You managed to prove that you are stronger.

name.en: Yes, I want to know what happens at the Burial Mound.

text.en:
What's out situation?

Vseslav with Catherina's minions stayed behind to guard the approaches. You, accompanied by the ghost of some strange sorceress, went into the depths.

You're probably wondering what happened next.

Well, first you had to decide which path to take. But perhaps I'll let this rebellious soul speak:

"The time has come. Before the Demon has a chance to raise a new army, we need to enter the tomb and challenge him! Your path lies through the thicket full of the undead. But that's not the worst part. There are only two ways to the tomb, and both of them are extremely dangerous.

One lies through the dead water. A huge ancient toad called Jam lives there.

The other road winds through the burial grounds where an ancient monster dwells. It once used to be a powerful necromancer. Tep was his name, I think... Oh, I see you know that name, don't you?

Choose your path wisely! And take this trinket. Use it to summon me at any time! I'll be with you all the time, unseen. I'll try and warn you if something is wrong. Best of luck to you!"

So what did you choose? Or maybe you defeated both enemies?

So what did you choose? Or maybe you defeated both enemies?

"All the words in the world can't express my gratitude. My friends found peace at last. The threat that was hanging over Umoir is gone. You did that. I can leave now.

We will never see each other again, so... Farewell. Fighting by your side was a great honor. While Sarnaut is under your protection, I'm not worried. My time is long gone. Your time is just beginning!" Those were Reniesta's parting words.

You reported back to Vseslav.

"The Demon is defeated?!

Praise you! And praise the ancestors! If it hadn't been for you, who knows what would've happened to Umoir. The whole world should hear about you. If you want that, I'll make it happen.

But I won't keep you. Great undertakings await you, I'm sure. We can defeat the remaining undead ourselves. Some are still wandering around. Which is understandable - who wants to spend an eternity in a damp grave?"

The Blight has lost its power since then. Slowly but surely it retreated from the Umoir lands. And the heroes have gone back to sleep in their tomb.

Being crushed by a toad... Not the most heroic death. The Blight creates astonishing creatures...

That's what the ghost that accompanied you said:

"It was dangerous even before the Blight, and now it's a real monster. Its name speaks for itself. It jams you into the ground, crushing your bones and flesh. Beware of its mighty croaking, too. There's a terrifying power in its voice. If you can, don't let it croak at all. Do something to distract it.

The battle with Jam will be long and exhausting, but if you keep looking upwards, you will avoid getting killed."

Of course, you made it past Jam.

name.en: Tell me about Brainum the Third

text.en:
Ogres, trolls, cyclopes, giants...

Sarn created many strong creatures. Fortunately for you, most of them are rather dull. That's putting it mildly. The Turses were the most intelligent of them, but the Elves wiped them out.

But here's an example of rare stupidity:

"Our next enemy makes me want to gloat. The Demon resurrected a cyclops named Brainum the Third - I guess he'd considered himself an aristocrat or something. Anyway, the Demon wanted to add this giant monster to his army, but he miscalculated. Brainum's greed was as massive as his strength. He's in the treasury at the moment, and it doesn't look like he's leaving it any time soon.

Of course, we could leave him to the locals. There are plenty of them to overpower him. Unfortunately, the only way to the tombs is through the treasury, and we don't have enough time to wait while they do it for us. You'll have to defeat him yourselves.

Brainum was stupid when he was still alive. Now he has no brain at all. Don't turn your back to him. Just one blow, and you're a wet spot on the ground! My advise is to split and take up positions in different corners of the treasury. His attention will be divided, and he will be running around the room... crushing everything in his way and shooting a magic beam from his eye. Look around. You might find something that will help you pacify him...

There's another danger I want you to remember about. If Brainum gets really mad, he can crush rocks and stones! He can easily bring down the whole tomb with you inside it. Don't let him focus on one target. Keep distracting him."

We won't be analyzing the family trees of overgrown monsters. The first two Brainums were trolls, if I remember correctly.

And that's how that dynasty ended. This is what the sorceress said about that:

"Ogres, trolls, cyclopes... I find their endless stupidity somewhat charming. Just imagine what it would be like if Brainum had brains? You'd be in deep trouble.

The tombs are near. There's just the final obstacle..."

Perhaps you and the others noticed that beliefs are different on the Kanian allods. The church spread its power throughout the Kanian Archipelago, and there's no other authority except the church on Forox, but it's not the same on Umoir. Maybe that's why there are so many sorcerers and witches here.

But we'll get back to it later. Let's talk about Morrana. That's what the ghost of that sorceress told you:

"When I was alive, I was a sorceress myself. I knew my limits, though, and I knew what I could do. Morrana is not like me...

Her powers are immense. Local peasants call her a Goddess of Death. She brought many woes upon these lands, poisoning the wells and killing the cattle with her plague. She might be more powerful than some of the Great Mages. I racked my brains over this whole thing for a while, but then it hit me.

The Scroll of Tensess! An ancient parchment inscribed with words of great power. I had a chance to see it during his lifetime... And let me tell you, many troubles happened because of this scroll, even if it bears the name of one of the best Great Mages. Morrana uses the magic contained in it to make her rituals more powerful. I don’t know where she got it and why she came to the Burial Mound with it. She probably wanted to enslave the Demon and become even stronger... She's so naive.

In any case, her arrival is a good thing for us. The scroll can come in handy in our fight against the Demon. I suggest we kill two birds with one stone - get the relic and save Sarnaut from this wicked witch. The secret to fighting mages of this level is to turn their sorcery against them. Carefully look around before the battle begins - is there anything around that can help us?

Morrana will surround herself with loyal servants. It's best to hit them with her own magic. But be careful - too much ancient magic can play a cruel trick on you."

Fortunately, even the Scroll of Tensess didn't help this witch.

"She's not the first one to fall because of her own arrogance. And not the last one. Whether fortunately or unfortunately, only time will show.

We're halfway through. The way to the inner chamber is open now. Keep your guard up: even I don't know what dangers lie ahead. Greatest warriors and most skillful mages are buried in these tombs. The Demon will surely summon them to its aid! On the other hand, not every creature it summons will obey it..."

The masks are discarded. The ghost turned out to be Reniesta, that “number 4 from Umoir”. The traitor whose name was forever tainted. The Demon and those he controlled were waiting ahead. I guess I'll let her speak:

"What's with the scroll and the cape, you ask? Tensess himself gave them to Skrakan. Why? For what purpose? I don’t know for sure. I suppose Tensess wanted to protect Skrakan during his experiment. But the Great Mage summoned an ancient demon to Umoir by mistake, and everything went pear-shaped. Animals turned into monsters, spirits went crazy... The Blight started then, do you understand? My friends stopped it. They defeated the demon and laid it to rest for all eternity.

At least that's what I thought... But then this stupid girl Catherina brought the damned thing back to life. And the whole thing started all over again. What's even worse, my friends, is that Danas, Fergard, and Naira were buried here together with their bitter enemy. The people of Umoir believed that this was the way to protect the dead from the corruption of demonic magic. That was a grievous mistake. Now the three of them will forever be the Demon's slaves.

I beg you to end their suffering. And be careful! They are experienced warriors, and it won't be easy to defeat them. Besides, the Demon has surely granted them a piece of his foul power. The scroll and the cape will help you in this battle. Use the scroll to break the connection between the heroes and the Demon. The cape will protect you from the deadliest attacks and spells.

Good luck! I will be praying for you... There's nothing else for me to do.

There was a glorious hero with us, Sir Brian. He was a paladin. His sword ended my life when I deceived my friends. His sword brought me back to life. Ancient magic works in mysterious ways..."

name.en: Ask about the battle with the Demon

text.en:
You were standing on the ancient burial ground, feeling the cold of the dungeons. Before you were the old heroes of Sarnaut, now slaves to a ruthless demon.

"Here they come, the heroes of Sarnaut! Blind fools coming to meet their death!" said Fergard.

"This scum dares to challenge Sarn? Challenge us?!" exclaimed Danas in outrage.

"They want to lay with us in the dark tombs of the Burial Mound? How can we deny them?" said Naira snidely.

And a terrible battle began - with those who had once been the defenders of Sarnaut. They had already defeated the Demon, but now they fought on its side.

As soon as you defeated them, it appeared from its grave:

"Your victories mean nothing, and you are nothing. Servants of Shadow who call themselves warriors of Light! Keep holding onto your trinkets! They did not help these fools. Raise, you slaves! You are doomed to fight... forever!"

"We... obey. We are one!" Those were the words of the fallen heroes.

But even the Demon was unable to fight off your onslaught.

"Well... So be it. Enjoy your victory while you can. Live in your bloody world! I have eternity!" Sarn's Demon disappeared after that.

Ancient bird maidens. Once upon a time, there were many of them, but alas, all good things disappear with time. There are just a few of them left. It's fortunate that some of them are on Umoir... But is it really? One of them has fallen under the influence of the Blight...

It's sad. There is not enough beauty in this world...

I'll let our guide speak:

We are close to the center of the Mound, the Heroes' tombs. One last guard stands in our way...

Have you heard about the bird of sorrow, Sirin? Two mystical birds lived here, on Umoir. Sirin and Gamayun. They spent centuries in this place, and saw both glorious and dark days. Gamayun sang songs of happiness and joy, while Sirin sang about sweet sorrow and hard lessons taught by the past.

As time went by, there was more sorrow than joy. I couldn't understand what made Sirin hide in these catacombs, but then it hit me! It was Catherina who imprisoned her in this gloomy place. Sirin was meant to sing about all the evil deeds of the queen, and to predict the end of Umoir. Who would possibly enjoy listening to this?

Unfortunately, Sirin stayed here for too long. The Demon's influence corrupted her body and mind. Now her songs are full of poison, and all she sings about is pain and death. We must end her suffering.

The problem is, she could use this area to her advantage. If she manages to fly high, it will be hard to defeat her - she can easily kill you all from up there. Try using her poisonous slime on her...

All birds keep their feathers clean. If you smear them with her own slime, she will be distracted and won't fly up. She will furiously beat her wings, and that's when you must strike."

Well, Sirin was defeated. And her death led to some revelations from your ghostly helper:

Sirin was singing songs of sorrow and despair, peering into souls and digging up secrets. I can't do this anymore! I have a confession to make. There's something I've been hiding from you.

My name is Reniesta. I first came to Umoir with my sworn sister and brothers a long time ago. We were trying to find out what happened to the Great Mage Skrakan. We saw a lot. We walked along many roads together. We fought shoulder to shoulder...

After everything we'd been through, I betrayed them. Betrayed my friends, my allies! For what? For some scroll and cape!"

This place attracts all kinds of vermin. The giant toad, ancient undead... And you haven't even reached the entrance yet! You want to know what happened next?

So, next enemy. That's what someone else said about it:

"Now it's time to face the most dreadful Blighted creature you can find on Umoir. To tell you the truth, it's not just the Blight that created it. It's a real magical conundrum.

Eye Stare is one of the oldest Treants in this place. Long ago it started dabbling in death magic, and its brethren exiled it to the Burial Mound. Which worked in its favor, because this place was exactly where it wanted to be. Plenty of dead bodies to raise, plenty of restless souls to let into its body. After a while, it lost its mind and decided it was the king of the local undead. When the Blight came, it readily accepted it, too. It became a loyal servant of the Demon. The locals were calling it Asura One Eye. Which doesn't tell you how terrifying it is. You'll see.

What really troubles me is its ability to turn invisible and attack from behind. It may invade your minds, so stay alert. Try using ashes from the urns here to reveal it when it's hidden, but be fast! The longer it stays disguised, the stronger it becomes.

Of course, Eye Stare also got itself some minions! It summoned the dead, and they answered its call. They can also become invisible, but luckily, ashes reveal them, too.

Do you understand now? This is where evil forces have been gathering.

It's a good thing you dealt with Eye Stare... You even got an interesting trophy.

"That's how Eye Stare keeps itself hidden! It had an ancient relic on it, a magical cape which I've seen before. Destiny's sense of humor is... peculiar.

Here's another joke. While you were fighting Eye Stare, guess who entered the Mound? Morrana herself. With the Scroll of Tensess in her hands! But first things first."

Interesting. The Blight is an incredible phenomenon. It's basically Life in a different form. It's too bad we can't coexist with it.

But there's a power that always opposes Life: Death. It's a good thing when your enemies help you defeat them. You don't understand?

Alright, let me tell you what that sorceress said:

"The monster maned Zomgie can raise the dead from their graves. It will be extremely difficult to defeat it since there's a huge cemetery around us. Thankfully, Blighted carnivorous plants don't like the living dead, so nature is going to be your ally in this fight against Death. It will distract the undead horde while you are fighting Zomgie.

So if you go through the Burial Grounds, you'll have to deal with Zomgie. Watch where it's looking. Its stare can be deadly."

name.en: Yes, I want to know what happens in the Winter Palace

text.en:
The Winter Palace... It's an interesting place. Built in the style of the Elven royalty. Alas, it has seen better days.

I'll repeat Eladia's words:

"This king of the Free Traders has built quite a palace! It's more of a museum, actually.

Did you know Ivan Chelezny is an esteemed collector? He gets his hands on all sorts of pieces of art, from silicon axes to elven statues, and the biggest part of his collection is stored in his country residence. I guess the old man spends his time looking at all his ill-gotten gains.

I hear there's so much gold in his treasury that the chests are overflowing with it. It's nice being a Free Trader, huh. The place is now occupied by the fanatics, so the museum is slowly turning into either a brothel or a nuthouse."

Well, if you hurry, you might save more than a few genuine artworks.

Eladia also said,

"Personally I think there are too many gods, demigods, and other mythic figures in our world. We need to reduce their ranks. Let's start with that big-mouthed goblin who calls himself the Prophet, and the dumb minotaur who called me... eh, never mind.

Any objections? No? That's what I thought!

Come on, gather your allies, and let's go!"

name.en: Yes, I want to know what happened to the Cultists of Order on Dane

text.en:
The war is over, but we still need to deal with the consequences, right? At least only Dane was affected.

And what do we have here? More cultists, only this time they worship Order? A strange goblin prophesying a new order?

Let me tell you what others have said:

"I knew there was someone more powerful behind the fanatics and the Prophet. At first I thought it could be a Great Mage, but when I heard them mention the Sculptor - and nobody told me about him for some reason! - everything became clear. However, I can only speculate about the purpose of their experiments. And my speculations are not comforting at all.

As you can remember, faith is a great power which can literally move mountains. The Architects - or should I say the Architect - is using the power of self-assertion. He believes in himself, and he is unflinching in his faith in the special purpose of his mind. But the Sculptor has lost that power when he detached himself from the whole. Now he is trying to compensate by creating monsters who look like him and have infinite faith in his power.

You see what the problem is? If the Sculptor succeeds in creating a sentient chimera using human and Architect flesh, and that creature will be a believer, we will face a catastrophe comparable in scale to the invasion of Dane! This is what the Prophet and the fanatics want - to create an army of chimeras who know no doubt or hesitation and believe in the divinity of the Sculptor."

We need to prevent that before it turns into a global problem... You want to hear the story?

name.en: Tell me about the aftermath of the events in the Winter Palace

text.en:
So the Cult of Order fell apart soon after it was formed. The Sculptor disappeared without a trace.

It looked like the war was over. The Architects' invasion was rebuffed, the Sculptor's schemes were foiled, but the threat of another attack loomed. For the Architects, failure in one of the worlds was just a delay of the inevitable. And then there was also Sarn. The mad god hasn't stopped trying to free himself, and every attempt put this world on the brink of destruction. And somewhere beyond the borders of this world, Nihaz was thirsting for revenge, his eyes glued to whatever was happening in Sarnaut.

There were also people willing to risk everything to save this world. Instead of waiting for the next cataclysm, they acted...

Finally, the last battle.

The battle for the Winter Palace ended with the battle against Bedlam - that very chimera which consisted of different parts and used the power of faith. Fortunately, this threat was dealt with before it became a crisis. However, you never met the Sculptor himself - he mysteriously disappeared.

"Oh my... Living statues in the yard - and a stone demigod on the roof! I must admit, I wasn’t expecting that. Now I'm even more eager to meet the Sculptor, but our friend is cautious... I’m sure we'll meet one day, and then I'll beat the living daylights out of him. But the threat was averted - the fanatics scattered, and the bandits surrendered to the authorities!"

Goblins. They are everywhere. They can be quite useful, but they cause a lot of harm.

You want to know about that Prophet, the self-proclaimed religious activist?

These are Eladia's words:

"The Prophet... I wonder where that crazy goblin came from. And how can people be such idiots?

Who in their right mind can believe a goblin on stilts wearing a colorful robe and carrying a dead Architect core under his arm? This is pure madness. Maybe that's his secret? If one combines pure madness with infinite faith, it can become a terrifying weapon in the hands of a skillful puppet master, and the Sculptor is a brilliant manipulator.

By the way, I heard there was a fire in a hospice right after the first Architects' attack on the Iron City. It was burned to the ground along with its patients and the staff which usually consists of goblins. Some of the bodies were not found. Maybe this twisted faith in the "holy Architects" was born in that fire?"

You mean Ivan's assistant? That Hoof? The traitor who tried to kill you? Greed has ruined so many lives.

This is what Eladia thinks about it:

"What about Hoof? He's just a greedy boor who will sell his own mother for a handful of gold. But now this animal wears an Assault Shell and carries a Meteorite hammer that can crush walls. Still, I don't think he'll be a problem for you. He's not Tep after all, and definitely not my father... But that rage of gold and blood can consume a being to the point where they feel nothing but blind fury whenever anyone tries to take their treasure from them. He will fight for his gold to the last drop of blood, that's for sure.

 If you defeat the Prophet and Hoof, the rest of the bandits and fanatics will scatter. There'll be no one standing between us and the Sculptor."

name.en: Tell me about the statues of elven heroes

text.en:
Statues of elven heroes? You don't need to hear their stories for now...

Eladia will tell you the rest:

"You mean those in the park?  I don't like them either. It's so weird to see elves without wings!

I read about those statues in a popular science magazine, "Science & Death", in the Supernatural section. The Historians discovered elven ruins on a distant allod which dates back to ancient times. The destroyed city was built by the Elves before the Change - which means long before the Cataclysm.

Just imagine how excited the archeologists were - the five elven statues remained intact among the ruins and ash! Too bad the ancient elves didn't like uninvited guests, so the second expedition found only withered remains of the first one at the feet of the statues. The second expedition was found dead on an Astral ship which was looted by pirates... The pirate ship was later discovered on a shore on Suslanger, and the statues turned up on the black market some time later. Eventually, an anonymous collector bought them.

Some say the statues are cursed, some say they contain ancient elven magic or even the Sparks of heroes of the past... It seems you'll be the one to uncover the truth."

Time... is too chaotic.

name.en: Tell me about the Melting Isle and whatever is happening there!

text.en:
I send everyone there twice a day. You can see the time in your own calendar. I can send you there from anywhere in Sarnaut, you don't have to come here, hehe. Just sign up for the Skirmish the way you usually do when you want to beat someone up at the Witch's Hollow or anywhere else.

You will need keys to open the chests. I'll give you ten per week, but you can save up a two-week supply of them if you want.

The rest is simple: go to the island alone, search for chests, fight other treasure hunters, take their loot, don't let others take it from you.

To open a chest, you need to wait until it "thaws". When you take a new treasure, your chests "freeze" again. When you run out of keys, I will bring you back. But when time runs out, all the participants will also be back, and their chests will immediately open.

name.en: Tell me about the return of the Melting Isle

text.en:
He he...

So, if you remember, this island was full of treasures buried somewhere in the ice. Over time, the island began to thaw, and treasures began to appear here and there, to the delight of greedy heroes. But all good things come to an end eventually. Over time, the Melting Isle was exhausted.

Forgotten and abandoned, it peacefully drifted through the astral plane. Until the "boom" on Suslanger. This Ambrosia of yours was thrown into space and, carried by the astral currents, began to spread... This stream affected the Melting Isle as well.

Divine energies caused temporal anomalies which revived the treasures you had plundered - June artifacts got filled with this power, turning into something else. And now, the island is again full of treasures.

Of course we will change the rules. Guild Wars? Pfft, boring. It's every man for himself! Of course, I know you, and you will definitely try to cheat... But it won't be easy!

name.en: How is the treasure hunt going?

text.en:
It's all very simple. I send players there twice a day. I can send you there from anywhere in Sarnaut, you don't have to come here. Just sign up for a Skirmish. You can see the time in your own calendar.

You will need keys to open the chests. I'll give you ten per week, but you can save up a two-week supply of them if you want.

The rest is simple: go to the island alone, search for chests, fight other treasure hunters, take their loot, don't let others take it from you.

To open a chest, you need to wait until it "thaws". When you pick up a new treasure, your chests "freeze" again. When you run out of keys, I will bring you back, sorry. But when time runs out, all the participants will also be back, and their chests will immediately open.

In addition, some surprises await you. The Ambrosia energy affecting the Melting Isle has created interesting orbs that boost you... or your enemies if they find them first. But there's a stipulation - if you have collected too many treasures, the orbs will no longer work for you.

And don't even try to go there with a group - it won't work!

Oh! Karah-Oki is the most useful thing invented by the Waterfolk aside from the Hurricane cocktail.
Legend has it that the origin of Karah-Oki is associated with Oki the Thunderous, the most loud-voiced singer, and the Great Turtle who is peacefully sleeping at the bottom of the ocean. Oki knew only one song. But what a song it was! You could say it's our anthem! When he sang - he always sang when he was drunk, and Oki drank like a fish - you could hear him far beyond the island. Poor Oki's loud singing really got on the Great Turtle's nerves. She became angry and punished him. The old woman cast oblivion on poor Oki, and he forgot the words of our only song! What a tragedy... But that didn't stop us! We wrote the words of the song on boards and showed them to Oki whenever he started singing.
In the end, the Turtle forgave Oki, and everything ended well. And singing when you have lyrics showed to you? It stuck, and we named it Karah-Oki!
Do you want to participate? I'll handle the music and you will sing. You can do it! I believe in you.
Don't know the lyrics? Not a problem! Just watch me when you sing. I will show you the lyrics, so you can sing heartily without having to worry about anything. There are no bad songs, just bad listeners!
Just don't get carried away, otherwise it won't take long to get hoarse from Karah-Oki
And what do I get? What valuables are you offering for my bugs and butterflies?

Want to race my crabs? My pleasure. Don't be too disappointed if you lose, tho.
To boost you just a bit, I'll give you a rocket. You'll fly over the water, the crabs will run on feet. But they'll be ahead anyway, no one has beaten them so far. Try and catch the tailwind with the rocket, it'll help. And if you do outfly them - which, to tell you the truth, I sincerely doubt - I will give you a good reward!

Later, beanpole! I'm not going to run to the village right now. I'm busy, understand? Affairs of the heart... You wouldn't believe the legs on this one! And she's got such pretty semi translucent webbings between those delicate toes... I would dry up the whole lake for my darling!
But you beanpoles will never understand our sense of beauty!
Well then, good luck to you. Be sure to come around again. Our villagers are always happy to see you.
Rawr!
But not in our world! You can't even die properly here, let alone resurrect. But you can use your Patronage abilities. They are so weird...

So, you want to save the innocent victim? How generous and kind of you! But before you rush to slaughter the lizards, let me give you a piece of advice.
The Altar and its guardians are protected by unknown and strange spell. With every single lizard slain, these protective powers weaken. You will see it yourself when you slay at least a dozen of them. If you manage to break their defenses, you will save the innocent victim and get the reward.
But you are not the only hero willing to save the girl. There are others who will try to get in your way using a special ability that pushes the competitors back from the victim. You can use it against your opponents, too, but every time you do so, the defenses will grow stronger, and you will have to kill the lizards again. Anyway, your rival's situation will become even worse...
Don't waste your time if you want to save the girl. Better let someone else do the job instead of leaving her to die!
Mausoleum of Sparks is waiting for you!
Hello seeker... Are you looking for truth and power? Don't try to fool me, I can see the hunger for glory in your eyes. With Master's permission I'll help you to meet your dreams!

name.en: Ask about the Trial of Bravery

text.en:
Trial of Bravery is your chance to earn glory in a ruthless battle, a chance to write your name into the list of Sarnaut's greatest heroes!
If you want to participate, gather your most faithful and experienced friends.
You will need the Shining Key to teleport into the Mausoleum of Sparks, an ancient structure created by Tep himself.
Tep used this Mausoleum for sacrifices. He extracted sparks from the bodies of his victims and placed them into his dreadful mechanisms to perform extraordinary magic!
The first mechanism can heal any wound after a spark absorption. The second one provides protection and speeds up the regeneration of magical powers. Using the third mechanism, you can feel a burst of energy embodied in a spark - your attacks will gain power and the energy will restore much quicker.
Our Master discovered the Mausoleum in the Astral depths and organized this Trial to find the strongest fighters.
Touch the stele in the center of the Mausoleum to start the Trial. Enemies will be coming in waves, you need to hold on as long as you can!

I'm not the leader, I just sit here and observe, I'm not doing anything! Don't kill me! I'll do anything, just don't kill me!

I'm quite useful! I know a lot, and I can do a lot! I'll tell you everything!

name.en: Proof, right... Give me the money!

What?! You're dead, wet-nose!
Have you been chewing on the local mushrooms? Grot will rip you apart and feed you to his beasts. Get out of here, instigator!
No... They are loyal to Grot, because he pays well, and this is a big order. It won't work! Now get out of here before they hang us!

name.en: Do you know who the customer is?

text.en: I don't, but if I did, I wouldn't tell you. What if you're working for the competition, trying to steal our order? Go away, eavesdropper!

name.en: I heard Caligula, the owner of the Skewer island, holds animal fights!

text.en:
That guy? Pfft... No, there's a bigger fish. Grot went pale in the face when he mentioned that one. He's not afraid of the goblin.

Listen... I've had enough of this talk! Others will come begging for food now! And you're in the way, so get out.

name.en: Why don't you just poison us?

text.en: Hey, did you make it all up? The debt? So you could pit us against each other? I'll show you!

name.en: Are you going to pay or not?

text.en: I'm going to hit you so you leave me alone!

name.en: The boatswain is asking when the food will be ready.

text.en: Soon. Would you stop asking? Damn freeloaders...

name.en: The boatswain also says you owe him a debt, so I'll take the money now.

text.en: What?! I owe him? Why would he think so? What's your proof?

name.en: I don’t know, he said that...

text.en: That bastard! Maybe I should add pepper to his food. He's lying, that dog!

name.en: Who keeps track of our gambling debts?

text.en: It's Grunt. Maybe you should ask him about the debt? Just start with a code phrase: "Evil maiden sank to the bottom"! Don't forget.

So what are you going to tell me? Nothing interesting, judging by your face!

Go bother someone else.

name.en: Stinky Zho asks about his debts!

text.en: Debts? Let's see, let's see... He doesn't owe anyone anything.
You can show Zirka this!
You? Who are you? Get out!

name.en: Stinky Zho demands to get paid right now!

text.en: Let him come, then. Why are you here? Are you an idiot? Here!

name.en: Evil maiden sank to the bottom! Stinky Zho sent me!

text.en: Aha! That's right. What does he want?

name.en: Stinky Zho wants to know when the rest will be paid!

text.en: The rest? We'll be paid when we're done with the job. Like he doesn't know. What has he been eating in his kitchen? Mushrooms?

name.en: Zho is afraid the customer will dupe us!

text.en: Is he an idiot? People like that aren't cheap - it's not some Izune bandit!

name.en: He needs guarantees, because no one on the team knows who that guy is...

text.en: So mistrustful. But oh well. I only heard half of it when the captain was speaking to him... to her, I mean. Our customer is Victoria Korleone, the head of the drug mafia that ate up all competition on Igsh, Suslanger, and Yakhch! She deals in psi-salt, which sells well these days. Quite a terrifying lady, worse than Tep, they say! But she keeps her word, so tell him not to worry, he'll be paid.

text.en:
This Ark is a true miracle! Trust me, I know something about miracles!

There are two Scrolls in the Ark. Read the first one to instantly reach level 115 and get all rubies and abilities available only to the mightiest heroes of Sarnaut.

Read the second Scroll to get a full set of rare equipment. The Ark also contains Droplets of Water of Life and Death to help you get used to your new abilities.

This Ark is a true miracle! Trust me, I know something about miracles!

There are two Scrolls in the Ark. Read the first one to instantly reach level 115 and get all rubies and abilities available only to the mightiest heroes of Sarnaut.

Read the second Scroll to get a full set of rare equipment. The Ark also contains a complete set of level 5 Runes, Droplets of Water of Life and Death to help you get used to your new abilities, a Twilight Wolf's collar for fast traveling around the world, a roomy Dragon Hide Backpack, a 36-slot Safe Deposit Box, and a 25-page Quest Log! Not to mention a significant amount of gold. Isn't that everything a hero needs?
